findings.title: Recognition crosses into visible witness
findings.claim: The revelation heard in the focus is recognized inwardly, and that recognition crosses the body's boundary as tears whose trace makes the response visible.
findings.mechanism: The focus hearing carries receptive understanding; the recognition word supplies identification by a sign, the overflow verb supplies easy excess beyond containment, and the tear-trace word gives that excess a visible path. Together the focus words turn inward recognition into an outwardly legible witness.
findings.reader_payoff: The tears become more than an intensifier of emotion: they let the reader see recognition leaving an observable trace before the spoken confession and witness petition.
findings.containment: The finding deepens the ordinary scene of hearing, recognizing, weeping, and speaking. It does not turn tears into a juridical proof or claim that every use of these words carries this composite relation.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run publication supplies the bounded relation, and every nominated branch is independently anchored in the focus surface.
